transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-15 16:00 UTC | Duration ~48m | Recording id ff-2026-11-15-aureline-01
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Aureline Head of Partnerships), Maya Chen (Aureline Enterprise Sales Dir), Carlos Ruiz (Aureline CISO)

Auto-summary (auto gen, may be imperfect): quick pipeline scrub, identify 6 joint targets, map risk (data residency, on-prem), agree next steps for pilot.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. we wanted this to be a focused sprint to map your top pipeline accounts to what we can co-sell and to surface any technical or legal blockers up front.
[00:20] Liam: yeah thanks, appreciate it. we have like, six deals that are high-priority this quarter that we think are a "fit", um, two of them are eu regulated financials, one's healthcare, rest are s-a-a-s platforms.
[00:35] Maya: quick clarity, when you say "fit" are we talking hosted-API first or are we already assuming on-prem for the big financial?
[00:45] Jordan: good q. our standard play is hosted for speed, Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Redwood Private (VPC/Customer-hosted) for the regulatory stuff. for the eu bank we expect Private or at least dedicated in eu region due to data residency and audit log needs.
[01:10] Carlos: from security side, main asks are SOC 2, SSO with SAML, encrypted logs at rest with customer-managed keys (we use Hashicorp), and audit trail retention of 2 years. do you have HSM/KMS integrations?
[01:30] Samira: yes, we integrate with KMS providers and H-S-M setups; our Private deployment supports customer-managed keys and audit logging. fyi sometimes the transcription on our docs shows H-S-M as h-s-m or, um, H S M but it's the same.
[01:45] Liam: ok good. cost question for the two fintechs: they push back on hosted cost, want to see unit economics. can we show them a model comparing hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[02:05] Jordan: absolutely, we'll put a joint pricing matrix. quick note — dedicated gives you predictable cost per token at scale but needs a commitment. hosted is flexible but unit cost higher. private has infra plus license. we'll model the three for each target.
[02:25] Maya: and route management — who owns the first touch? Aureline or Redwood?
[02:33] Jordan: typical co-sell: partner (Aureline) owns discovery and intro, Redwood does technical deep-dive + pilot. revenue routing and influenced vs closed-won will be in joint MOU. we'll draft the one-pager.

[03:00] Topics: pipeline mapping; risk triage per account; pilot scope; perf benchmarks; enablement docs.

[03:30] Liam: let me walk through account 1 — "Fenwick Bank" (EU retail bank). deal size potential 350k ARR. tech constraints: no data can leave EU, customer wants private deployment on their Azure tenancy or host in EU region with strict key control.
[03:55] Samira: for Fenwick we can do Redwood Private deployed into their VNet, or Dedicated capacity in our eu cluster with customer-managed keys, depending on their compliance team. private will require network peering and certs, and a short engagement for the install.
[04:20] Carlos: will that require an on-prem appliance? they have a legacy system, might want full air-gapped.
[04:30] Samira: if they want fully air-gapped that's a heavier lift and more time — likely a separate project. for many fintechs, Private on Azure with strict KMS + PCI controls is sufficient.

[05:00] Jordan: action wise — we should identify which of the two fintechs actually require air-gapped vs just eu-residency. Liam can confirm.
[05:12] Liam: yep will do.

[06:00] Maya: account 2 is "Helio Health" — big healthcare payer. they require BAAs and specific PHI handling, plus a SOC 2 Type II. they also want a trial for clinicians with a max latency of 200 ms to not disrupt workflows.
[06:25] Samira: latency target's doable with Dedicated in region and batching tuned. we'll propose latency/cost tradeoffs — smaller batch for latency-sensitive flows, larger batch for throughput. but note: generation length matters — we saw spikes when context windows are long.
[06:50] Jordan: we can show the perf tradeoff with two sample prompts. Samira's team will run a 20k-token benchmark with the real prompts and paste results in the shared sheet.

[07:20] Maya: who will own the benchmarks? Aureline or Redwood?
[07:26] Samira: Redwood will run the baseline and share. if Aureline wants to run on customer infra afterward we can hand off the script.

[08:00] Carlos: security question — how immutable are audit logs? can we prove tamper evidence?
[08:10] Priya: yes we have append-only audit logging in Private, and the hosted product stores signed logs with retention config. we can provide sample logs and audit schema.
[08:25] Carlos: okay please send sample schema.

[09:00] Jordan: switching to pipeline prioritization — we mapped six accounts; we propose prioritizing three for pilot: Fenwick Bank, Helio Health, and "Nimble Commerce" (SaaS marketplace). the others are longer-term.
[09:25] Liam: agreed, Nimble is quick if we do hosted for initial test; they have no residency constraints and are price-sensitive.

[10:00] Maya: Nimble's technical contact asked about model options — Redwood provides a model catalog, but can we support customer-specified models or bring-your-own?
[10:15] Samira: we support curated open models and variants; BYOM is possible on Private with gating. for hosted we typically offer our verified model catalog. BYOM on hosted is limited due to security.

[10:45] Jordan: competitor callout — some of these accounts already kicked the tires with Anthropic and Cohere. common objections were cost and latency for small requests.
[11:05] Liam: yes and some were worried about vendor lock in. how do we handle that in the playbook?
[11:14] Jordan: we emphasize multi-model routing, transparent performance docs, and a rollback plan. also partner-led introductions reduce lock-in concerns since Aureline co-sells.

[12:00] Samira: tech detail: we recommend prefix caching and KV cache strategies for chat-style apps to reduce per-token costs. sometimes sales calls hear "K-V cash" which is funny in a transcript but it's KV cache.
[12:25] Maya: can you explain prefix caching to our reps in a one-pager?
[12:30] Priya: yes we'll include caching notes in the enablement doc.

[13:00] Jordan: pricing mechanics — propose a joint discount structure for deals closed via Aureline during pilot window (Q4). we'll draft a joint pricing matrix where active pilot accounts get a discount for first 6 months plus co-sell credit.
[13:25] Liam: that helps sell. we need an example TCO vs hosted baseline to show procurement.

[14:00] Samira: for TCO we'll output example per-token and infra costs for 3 months at anticipated qps. also note: quantization and batching options can reduce GPU usage.

[15:00] Maya: there was a customer that asked about function calling and tool integration — do you support function/tool calling for structured output?
[15:14] Samira: yes, we support function/tool calling and structured outputs. for some regulated workflows it's safer to use structured outputs and schema enforcement. we'll include examples.

[16:00] Jordan: ok moving to risk mapping — list of potential blockers: data residency (2 accounts), on-prem requirement (1 account), SOC2/BAA evidence (several), network peering/cert timelines, and procurement lead time. who wants to call out anything else?
[16:24] Carlos: encryption in transit + at rest, key rotation policy and proof we can rotate without downtime.
[16:35] Samira: we can show rotation docs and a maintenance window plan.

[17:15] Liam: timeline check: can we get a pilot running in 3 weeks for Nimble and Fenwick at least?
[17:25] Jordan: Nimble yes (hosted), Fenwick likely needs 4-6 weeks if Private/on-prem; if they accept Dedicated eu-region we might compress to 3 weeks but still need legal sign-offs.

[18:00] Priya: enablement plan: we'll produce a 1-pager for AE/SDR handoff, a technical runbook for SEs, and a short recorded demo for Aureline sales. Priya to lead enablement doc.

[19:00] Jordan: let's confirm deliverables: 1) co-sell one-pager + joint pricing matrix; 2) perf benchmark (20k tokens) and result sheet; 3) enablement pack (slides + 1-pager + demo); 4) security artifacts (SOC2 cert, audit log schema, KMS integration docs).
[19:25] Maya: that looks good.

[20:00] Samira: on the perf test — small gotcha, the test will show different latency depending on prompt length and context window. we'll include both chat-style and single-turn prompts.

[21:00] Jordan: ok, any questions on lead routing, MOU or revenue split? we should keep the MOU simple for pilots. maybe revenue influenced vs closed-won — default 50/50 credit for first pilot period?
[21:25] Liam: Aureline prefers referral fee for first pilot or a credit on the first invoice. we can negotiate the exact split but want simplicity.

[22:00] Jordan: we'll propose a simple referral credit for pilot closes and outline the longer-term revenue share once pilots convert.

[23:00] Carlos: one more security note — we need to run a brief questionnaire. can you point to an example security questionnaire or do we send our own?
[23:12] Priya: send your questionnaire and we'll fill it; we can also provide our standard security pack proactively.

[24:00] Jordan: great. quick recap: Jordan to share one-pager + pricing by 11/18, Samira to run perf tests and upload results by 11/22, Priya to produce enablement by 11/19, Liam to confirm pilot account list by 11/20, Carlos to send security questionnaire and receive filled pack by 11/24.
[24:40] Liam: ok sounds good.

[25:00] Closing notes: references shared during call: https://redwood.example.com/partner-one-pager (placeholder), shared benchmark sheet at https://docs.example.com/spreadsheets/aureline-benchmarks (placeholder).

[25:30] Jordan: thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the technical kickoffs after the artifacts are shared.
[25:45] Maya: thanks everyone.
[26:00] (meeting ends — last ~2 minutes had small side chats about scheduling that didn't capture well)
